combination.tip: Auto-tagged: this band is a combination (sum) mode, not a fundamental.

computational.tip: A calculation rather than a measured spectrum. On one claim it says that claim is calculated (e.g. DFT); on a band it is auto-tagged and says every claim behind it is, with no measurement at all. Not the same as unreferenced, where nothing has been recorded; the chart fades the two from separate switches so you can ask for measured evidence alone.

degenerated.tip: Two or more vibrational modes coincide at the same frequency and share one observed band.

direct-dosing.tip: Species generated by dosing/adsorbing its own desorbed counterpart directly (e.g. formate from formic acid), not via a genuine surface reaction.

infrared.tip: Umbrella switch: the band has at least one infrared claim, whichever sampling geometry it used. It is a legend control rather than a label, so it is not drawn on the band or the claim, where the specific chip (DRIFTS, transmission, ATR and the rest) already says it. The one exception is a claim whose source said only IR (or FTIR) and no geometry: that claim's technique is infrared itself, and then the chip is a label like any other.

drifts.tip: Measured by diffuse reflectance infrared spectroscopy (DRIFTS).

raman.tip: A Raman shift rather than an infrared absorption: the same vibrational energy, seen through the polarizability rather than the dipole.

srs.tip: Spontaneous Raman scattering, said in so many words by the source. The scattering happens by itself from a single laser, rather than being driven by a second beam as in the coherent techniques (CARS, stimulated Raman). It sits under "raman" the way DRIFTS sits under the infrared, and plain "raman" stays the tag for a paper that does not specify.

irras.tip: Measured by infrared reflection absorption spectroscopy: grazing incidence off a flat, usually single-crystal sample in vacuum. The surface selection rule applies, so only dipole components along the surface normal absorb and a missing band may mean a mode lying flat rather than a species that is absent.

seiras.tip: Surface-enhanced infrared absorption on a metal-film electrode, nearly always through an ATR prism (Kretschmann geometry). Only dipoles normal to the metal are enhanced, and the spectra are differences against a reference potential, so a band pointing down is a species consumed.

pm_irras.tip: IRRAS with the polarisation modulated between s and p, which subtracts the isotropic gas-phase and window background and lets reflection measurements work outside vacuum.

emission.tip: The hot sample is the infrared source rather than something the beam passes through; used where a bed is too opaque or too hot for the other geometries.

mioirs.tip: Mixed Isotope Operando Infrared Spectroscopy: the cell is fed a deliberately mixed isotopic stream, a little ¹³CO in ¹²CO, so neighbouring adsorbates stop vibrating at the same frequency and the dipole coupling between them is detuned. The odd chip of the infrared family, naming what went into the cell rather than how the beam reached the sample, because a decoupled adlayer is a different measurement whichever geometry recorded it. Proposed by Monai in 2024; nothing in the atlas carries it yet.

fermi-resonance.tip: Auto-tagged: this band is one half of a Fermi-resonance doublet with another band.

frustrated-mode.tip: A free gas-phase rotation/translation that becomes a restoring-force vibration once the molecule is adsorbed.

fundamental.tip: Auto-tagged: the v = 0 → 1 transition of a normal mode, the first step rather than a multiple or a sum. A rotational branch is still a fundamental, and so is an IR-inactive mode.

transmission.tip: Measured in transmission through a self-supporting wafer, rather than by diffuse reflectance.

free.tip: Auto-tagged from the claim's form: the molecule on its own, as a gas, as the liquid itself or isolated in a matrix, rather than held by anything.

dissolved.tip: Auto-tagged from the claim's form: a solute in a liquid, such as CO₂ or formate in an electrolyte. Solvation moves the band and removes the rotational structure, so this is not a free-molecule value.

adsorbed.tip: Auto-tagged from the claim's form: the species held on a surface; which surface is in its own site badge. It does not say whether the species adsorbed intact or as a fragment: that is the band-level "undissociated".

surface.tip: Auto-tagged from the claim's form: a group belonging to the solid itself, such as a surface hydroxyl or a metal hydride, rather than something adsorbed on it.

lattice.tip: Auto-tagged from the claim's form: a vibration or a defect of the solid itself, such as a lattice overtone or a vacancy absorption.

in vacuum.tip: Auto-tagged from the claim's medium: measured in an evacuated or ultra-high-vacuum cell with no gas let in, as for single-crystal reflection work.

in gas.tip: Auto-tagged from the claim's medium: measured under a gas atmosphere, from a fraction of a mbar of dosed gas to a flowing feed at pressure. On an adsorbed band it describes the surroundings, not the species.

in liquid.tip: Auto-tagged from the claim's medium: measured in a liquid or an electrolyte, as at an electrode. Adsorbates there feel the solvent and the electrode potential, so their positions differ from the same species under a gas.

in matrix.tip: Auto-tagged from the claim's medium: isolated in a frozen noble gas (neon or argon) at a few K. Effectively the free molecule with its rotation quenched, but the host still shifts the position by a few to twenty cm⁻¹.

ir-inactive.tip: Symmetry-forbidden in IR; included for context even though not directly observed. It also covers the other half of the branch rule: an O or S branch is a ΔJ = ±2 step, which one photon cannot drive, so those branches exist in Raman and not in the infrared. Drawn hollow when the chart is set to IR.

isotope-labeling.tip: This source used isotope substitution as evidence for the assignment (the band itself is the ordinary, natural-abundance one).

isotope.tip: Umbrella switch: the band is a labelled twin of another one rather than the ordinary molecule. A legend control rather than a label, so it is not drawn on the band itself, where the substitution chip (deuterium, carbon-13, oxygen-18) already says it and says which.

carbon-13.tip: This band is the ¹³C-substituted twin of another band in the atlas, not the ordinary molecule.

oxygen-18.tip: This band is the ¹⁸O-substituted twin of another band in the atlas, not the ordinary molecule.

deuterium.tip: This band is the deuterated twin of another band in the atlas: same mode, heavier hydrogen. Drawn hatched.

to-be-revised.tip: Something on this band does not add up and has not been resolved yet: a claim that may sit on the wrong band, or an assignment that needs the source read again. Not a caveat about the chemistry, a note that the entry itself is unfinished.

misassignment-warning.tip: A known trap: this position is easily assigned to the wrong species, or read as a surface signal when it is not one (gas-phase absorption in the beam path).

undissociated.tip: The species sits on the surface intact rather than broken into a fragment: adsorbed methanol CH₃OH* as against the methoxy CH₃O* it dissociates into. That is a property of the species wherever it is seen, so it is a band tag. Not the same as the per-claim "adsorbed", which only says one measurement was made on a surface: every methoxy claim is adsorbed, and methoxy is not undissociated.

overtone.tip: Band is an overtone of a lower fundamental, not the fundamental itself.

raman-inactive.tip: Forbidden in Raman: the vibration leaves the polarizability unchanged (for gas CO₂, every infrared band, by the mutual exclusion rule), or, for a linear molecule's P and R branches, the rotational change is one Raman does not allow. Note the rule is one-directional: O and S never appear in the infrared, but P and R are not Raman-forbidden in general. Raman reaches ΔJ = 0, ±1, ±2 for a symmetric top, a spherical top, or a linear molecule in a degenerate vibration; it is only a linear molecule in a non-degenerate vibration that is restricted to O, Q and S. Drawn hollow when the chart is set to Raman.

rotational.tip: Auto-tagged: one line of a pure rotational spectrum, where nothing vibrates and the molecule only turns faster. Labelled by the level it starts from. Not a branch among several, which is what the vibrational bands get: pure rotation only ever gives an S branch, so what this band has siblings in is the single branch itself, line by line.

rotational-branches.tip: Auto-tagged: this band is one part of a transition that rotation has split, and it has siblings. Usually that means one branch of several, and which letters appear depends on the technique and the rotor: P/Q/R in the infrared, O/Q/S for a linear molecule in Raman, all five for a symmetric or spherical top. For a pure rotational spectrum it means something narrower, since there is only ever an S branch: the siblings are then the individual lines of it, one per starting level.

site-sensitive.tip: Band position shifts meaningfully with adsorption site or surface composition.
